event.title: Trump and Putin Meet Ahead of Trilateral Talks with Xi Jinping in China
event.canonical_title: Trump and Putin Meet Ahead of Trilateral Talks with Xi Jinping in China
event.summary: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, shaking hands as they prepare for their first trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The meeting comes amid discussions on global security, energy, and finance. While the Kremlin indicated an informal meeting took place, it remains unclear how the ongoing war in Ukraine will be addressed during the talks.

timeline.title: Leaders of China, US, and Russia Hold Historic Trilateral Talks in Shenzhen
timeline.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin convened for a historic trilateral summit in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The leaders described the discussions as 'fruitful' and 'open and candid,' although no concrete agreements were reached. The meeting highlighted the ongoing tensions in the US-China trade war, with both Xi and Trump acknowledging the need for cooperation to safeguard world peace.

event_overview.title: About US-Russia Relations
event_overview.subject: US-Russia Relations
event_overview.summary: U.S.-Russia relations encompass diplomatic, security, economic and arms-control issues between two nuclear-armed permanent members of the UN Security Council. The Shenzhen meetings place a U.S.-Russia leader-level engagement within China’s 2026 APEC host year, alongside a separate three-leader discussion involving China.

facts.label: Diplomatic relations
facts.value: The United States recognized the Russian Federation as the Soviet Union’s successor on December 25, 1991, and established diplomatic relations with it on December 31, 1991.

facts.label: Meeting setting
facts.value: China hosted APEC in 2026, and Shenzhen hosted the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting on November 19, 2026; APEC describes itself as a forum of 21 member economies.

facts.label: Format and participants
facts.value: The talks included a separate Trump-Putin meeting and a subsequent face-to-face meeting among U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the margins of the Shenzhen APEC gathering.

facts.label: Arms-control context
facts.value: New START, the bilateral treaty limiting U.S. and Russian strategic offensive arms, entered into force on February 5, 2011 and was extended through February 4, 2026; its expiration makes nuclear-risk and arms-control issues a central context for later leader-level discussions.

facts.label: Economic and legal context
facts.value: U.S. Russia-related sanctions operate through multiple executive and statutory authorities, including Ukraine-/Russia-related measures, Russian Harmful Foreign Activities sanctions and CAATSA; the scope of restrictions and licenses varies by program.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the November 18-19, 2026 leader meetings in China, not the full history of U.S.-Russia diplomacy, sanctions, the war in Ukraine, or all APEC proceedings.
